hidden_target.material_initial_state: As-cast Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 (at.%) refractory high-entropy alloy produced by vacuum levitation melting and remelted 5–6 times under high-purity Ar; it was a single-phase BCC solid solution (lattice constant 3.411 Å) with approximately 100 μm equiaxed grains and a weak dendritic/interdendritic elemental distribution.
hidden_target.intervention: The alloy was cold rolled longitudinally in multiple passes to 20%, 50%, or 80% thickness reduction (0.1 mm reduction per pass; roll linear velocity 600 mm/s). The 80%-rolled alloy was subsequently annealed for 20 min at 650, 700, 750, or 800 °C.
hidden_target.conditions: Room-temperature tensile tests were conducted at 1 mm/min with three tests per processing condition. Phase and microstructure were evaluated by XRD, SEM/TEM, and EBSD, including inverse-pole-figure, grain-orientation-spread, grain-boundary-misorientation, and texture analyses.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: Increasing rolling reduction elongated and oriented the grains, generated dislocation tangles/walls and an increasing fraction of low- and medium-angle boundaries (0.530 as-cast to 0.849 at 80% reduction), and produced a strong <101>(111) texture while retaining the single BCC phase. Annealing promoted recovery and necklace-like recrystallization, reduced dislocation and low-/medium-angle-boundary densities, and increased the recrystallized fraction from 15% at 650 °C to 49.1% at 800 °C.
hidden_target.mechanism: Cold-rolling-induced work hardening and dislocation blocking, together with texture and the alloy's intrinsic lattice-distortion/solid-solution strengthening, impede dislocation motion and raise strength at the expense of ductility. Higher-temperature annealing enhances atomic diffusion, dislocation rearrangement and annihilation, and nucleation/growth of strain-free recrystallized grains, weakening dislocation/interface strengthening but facilitating slip and restoring ductility.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-cast alloy, progressively greater cold rolling increases tensile strength but decreases elongation. Relative to the unannealed 80%-rolled condition and lower annealing temperatures, increasing annealing temperature decreases strength and increases plasticity through recovery and recrystallization.
hidden_target.baseline: The primary rolling baseline was the as-cast alloy, with tensile strength 1007 MPa, yield strength 562 MPa, and elongation 23%. For the annealing comparison, the baseline was the 80%-rolled, unannealed alloy, with tensile strength 1408 MPa and elongation 10.5%.
hidden_target.boundary: The reported trends apply to the studied single-phase Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 alloy under 20–80% room-temperature cold rolling and, for the 80%-rolled state, 20 min annealing at 650–800 °C. Full recrystallization above 800 °C and high-temperature tensile performance were not tested.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: Tensile stress–strain testing discriminated changes in tensile strength and elongation, while EBSD quantified grain morphology, boundary misorientation and GOS-derived recrystallized fraction; TEM assessed dislocation agglomeration and XRD/TEM diffraction checked phase retention.
hidden_target.actual_result: At 80% rolling reduction, tensile strength reached 1408 MPa, about 40% above the as-cast value of 1007 MPa, while elongation fell from 23% to 10.5%; the low-/medium-angle-boundary fraction increased from 53.0% to 84.9%, and the paper reports a 3.2-fold dislocation-density increase. After 20 min annealing, tensile strength declined from 1251 MPa at 650 °C to 1069 MPa at 800 °C, while elongation rose from 11% to 17%. The recrystallized fraction increased from 15% at 650 °C to 49.1% at 800 °C, with more ductile dimples at 750–800 °C; the alloy remained single-phase BCC after rolling.
